<findings>
<finding task="0"><quote>A check uses a version other than the `[packages]` value only through an `[[override]]` entry with four keys: `gate`, `package`, `version` and `reason`.</quote><plan>## Global Constraints

Every task's requirements include this section.</plan><fix>Add the `## Review Focus` section that the header requires, between Global Constraints and Decisions. It is missing. List the five uncovered failure modes most likely to affect a user, and pin each with a test in the task whose code would fail:
1. A user runs a skill script through the `~/.claude/skills` symlink and the script floats (S4). Test in Task 4.
2. A worktree made before the merge silently inherits the freeze date (N1). Test in Task 16.
3. `drift`'s second pass runs on a new Python where a gate has no wheels, and the report shows exit 2 or 1 with the package named. Test in Task 8.
4. `check` flags prose such as "Python 3" or a bare year next to a package name. Add a no-false-positive test in Task 9.
5. A `bump` that moves a pin under a `[[override]]` still keeps the override. Test in Task 3.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>| D1 | How the checks choose versions | Exact pins in one file, plus a separate drift run on the newest releases. Not a floating gate |</quote><plan>- **D1** (owner, plan review, 2026-10-21): Q1. Task 1 re-runs the uv probe.</plan><fix>The plan's Labels section defines D1 to D8 as the spec's owner decisions, then reuses D1 to D8 in `## Decisions` for different plan-review decisions. Every "D2" or "D4" reference is now ambiguous, including "Spec-level decisions (D1, D2, D6)" and "the case that D2 ... makes visible". Number the plan-review decisions D9 to D16, or rename the spec ones, and update every reference.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>Status:** approved by the owner on 2026-10-21, after a section-by-section design review and a review of the written text.</quote><plan>The decisions that need you are Q1 to Q8 above. The defaults are marked, and the tasks are written for them.</plan><fix>`## Decisions` already records the owner's approval of every Q1 to Q8 default, so the handoff, the "Owner questions (answer at plan review, before execution)" heading and the conditionals that remain ("If the owner answered Q2 with the alternative…", "only with Q6's default") contradict it. Change the heading to "Owner questions (decided at plan review)". Drop the remaining conditionals, and drop the handoff's request for answers.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>The plan writes each test before its code (red, then green).</quote><plan>- [ ] **Step 3: Write the module.** Create `build/versions.py`.</plan><fix>This fails the Proportion check. The plan is many times longer than the spec because it writes out full bodies for the probe script (Task 1), `versions.py` (Tasks 2, 3, 5, 8, 9), `versions_check.py`, and the Task 11 helper scripts, and the signatures and tests already determine most of that code. Replace the bodies with signatures, Interfaces and test assertions. Keep code only for the non-obvious algorithms: `citation_regex` and `judge`, the cutoff rule, and `rewrite`'s comment-preserving edit. Keep the probe rows as a table of the expected results rather than as a script.</fix></finding>
<finding task="1"><quote>Re-probe the uv behaviors in the Inventory (items 2 to 6, the shadow file under `skills/`, and nested-worktree inheritance) on the uv version of the day. Record the results in `specs/verification/`. If a behavior changed, stop and bring the change to the owner before going on.</quote><plan>- [ ] **Step 1: Create the probe script.** Write this file exactly.</plan><fix>Replace the roughly 200-line transcript with the probe table: id, the command shape, the expected result and the PASS/FAIL/RECORD rule. Also state the `--no-cache` requirement and the out-of-repo temp tree. The implementer writes the script from that table.</fix></finding>
<finding task="3"><quote>A joint resolve that fails in `bump` or `drift` names the packages in conflict. This is how a conflict under D2 (one version per package) becomes visible.</quote><plan>raise VersionsError(f'resolve step: joint resolve of {", ".join(requirements)} on Python '
                            f'{python_version} failed:\n{done.stderr.strip()}')</plan><fix>The error lists every requirement, not the packages in conflict. The test only checks that a two-package input appears in the message. Extract the conflicting names from uv's resolver output (the `Because X … and Y …` lines), intersect them with `[packages]`, and name only those. Add a stub-uv test with a three-package input in which only two conflict, and assert that the third is not named.</fix></finding>
<finding task="9"><quote>Each script's `requires-python` must match the Python floor in its `SKILL.md` `compatibility:` line. The dev Python must satisfy each floor.</quote><plan>- **D4** (owner, plan review, 2026-10-21): Q4. The floors rule fails when a script needs a higher Python than its skill promises or than the dev Python. A lower script floor passes. Applied in: Task 9.</plan><fix>Relaxing "must match" to "must not exceed" changes what the spec requires, so it is a spec-level decision, but it is logged as plan-level. Add an amendment step (A4), with an exact replace-this-with-that block for R4.1 item 4, tagged `(owner, plan 66, 2026-10-21)`. Change the Decisions line to "Applied in: Task 9 (spec amendment A4)".</fix></finding>
<finding task="11"><quote>The known stale citations are the Polars, Altair and plotly lines, `skills/bayesian-workflow/references/model-comparison.md:130`, `references/model-criticism.md:196` and `skills/deep-learning/references/frameworks.md:94-95`.</quote><plan>| `recommend-visualization` "Polars 1.42" (five places) | `HISTORICAL` with the reason "verified on 1.42, not re-checked on 2.x", and a deferred item. The claims need real charts in four libraries |</plan><fix>The "Altair 6.2" and "plotly 6.8" citations go unhandled. Their latest releases are 6.3.0 and 7.1.0, but `check` will never flag them, because `[cited]` is seeded with the same stale values. Add them to Task 11: either re-check them on the latest releases and update both the prose and `[cited]`, or record "verified on 6.2/6.8, not re-checked on 6.3.0/7.1.0" with a deferred item. Neither option may leave `[cited]` silently matching stale prose.</fix></finding>
<finding task="13"><quote>`build/check_jax_examples.py` and its documented command: they install `stack('jax-cpu')` in place of `--with-requirements specs/verification/32-jax-cpu.txt`.</quote><plan>uv run python build/versions.py run jax-cpu -- python build/check_jax_examples.py skills/deep-learning/</plan><fix>The old command ran under `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu`, and both the new CLAUDE.md command and the `jax cpu examples` step in Task 8's `verify_steps` drop it. Swapping the install source must not change the platform. Keep the `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu` prefix on the documented command, and have `verify_steps` and `drift` set `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu` in that step's environment. Add a test assertion for it in Task 8.</fix></finding>
<finding task="13"><quote>**`run_suites.py` tests.** `build/test_run_suites.py` and `build/test_check_frontmatter.py:434` build their expected commands from the file, not from a `3.13` literal.</quote><plan>The sweep also changed the sample command text in `build/test_check_frontmatter.py` (R7 names its line 434). That test checks only the runner word, so it keeps passing.</plan><fix>R7 requires this test to build its expected command from `build/versions.toml`, and deleting the flag text does not do that. Add a step in Task 7 that is RED first: it rewrites `test_check_frontmatter.py:434` to derive the interpreter and the cutoff from `versions.load()`. Also derive the fixture `dev` value in `test_run_suites.py`'s `VERSIONS_TOML` from `versions.load().dev_python`, not from a `'3.13'` literal.</fix></finding>
</findings>
